messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Hindi, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Hindi line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | l'ora | “the hour” (temporal unit) | क्षण | “moment / hour” | OK | | del | genitive “of the” | का | “of” | OK | | tempo | “time” | समय | “time” | OK | | e | coordinating “and” | और | “and” | OK | | la (before *dolce*) | definite article (fem.) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | dolce | “sweet, pleasant” | मीठा | “sweet” | OK | | stagione | “season” | मौसम | “season” | OK | | ma | adversative “but” | पर | “but” | OK | | non (1st) | negation of the comparative clause | नहीं | “not” | OK | | sì | intensifier “so” (as in “so that”) | ऐसा | “so / such” | OK | | che (subordinator) | “that” introducing clause | कि | “that” | OK | | paura | “fear” | भय | “fear” | OK | | non (2nd) | negation of the verb “give” | न | “not” (before verb) | OK | | mi | indirect object “to me” | मुझे | “to me” | OK | | desse | subjunctive “give” | दे | “give” | OK | | la (before *vista*) | definite article (fem.) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | vista | “sight, view” | दृश्य | “sight / view” | OK | | che (relative) | “which” | जो | “which” | OK | | m'apparve | “appeared to me” (verb) | प्रकट हुआ | “appeared” | OK | | d'un | “of a” (partitive) | एक | “a / one” | OK | | leone | “lion” | शेर | “lion” | OK |
### Items to Note - **UNNECESSARY**: the Italian definite article **la** appears twice (before *dolce* and before *vista*) but Hindi does not use articles, so they are omitted. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected in the lexical mapping. - Punctuation mismatch (Hindi line 45 ends with “।” instead of “.”) is a punctuation issue, not a word‑level error, and therefore is not listed here.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Hindi script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Hindi text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 43: - Original: समय का क्षण और मीठा मौसम; - Issue: none - Corrected: समय का क्षण और मीठा मौसम;
- Line 44: - Original: पर ऐसा नहीं कि भय मुझे न दे - Issue: none - Corrected: पर ऐसा नहीं कि भय मुझे न दे
- Line 45: - Original: वह दृश्य जो मेरे सामने एक शेर के रूप में प्रकट हुआ। - Issue: contains unnecessary words “मेरे सामने”, “के रूप में”; wording not faithful to source - Corrected: वह दृश्य जो मुझे शेर दिखाया।
``` समय का क्षण और मीठा मौसम; पर ऐसा नहीं कि भय मुझे न दे वह दृश्य जो मुझे शेर दिखाया। ```
